## Summary of Work Done
I was in the process of validating a German grammar question about the null article (Nullartikel) with country names after the preposition "nach". I analyzed the explanations for all five wrong answers.

## Analysis Completed
The question asks learners to fill in the article (or "—" for null article) in "Wir fliegen morgen nach ___ Spanien." The correct answer is "—" (null article) because "Spanien" is a neuter country name that takes no article after "nach".

Most explanations are accurate, but the explanation for "ein" contains a misleading element - it states "„ein" ist der Nominativ" as if case were the primary reason it's wrong, when the real issue is that no article is used at all with neutral countries after "nach". This could confuse learners into thinking the dative form "einem" might be acceptable.
